newsitem.title: USA: ITEQ and Astrotech to merge.
newsitem.headline: ITEQ and Astrotech to merge.

text.p: ITEQ Inc said Wednesday that it and Astrotech International Corp entered into a merger agreement whereby Astrotech will be merged into ITEQ.
Subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, the shareholders of Astrotech will receive 0.93 ITEQ shares for each Astrotech share, the release said.
Astrotech shares closed Wednesday at 7-1/2. ITEQ shares closed at 11-3/4.
The transaction should be immediately accretive to ITEQ's earnings, the company said.
ITEQ issued a news release saying that the boards of directors of both ITEQ and Astrotech approved entering into the merger agreement.
In its most recent fiscal year ended September 30, 1996, Astrotech reported net income of $4 million on sales of $122 million, the release said.
The transaction will be accounted for as a pooling-of-interests, the release said.
The combined companies will be a significantly more efficient operation with annual pre-tax cost savings expected to exceed $2.5 million, the release said.
Since 1989 Astrotech has acquired eight companies and has about 1,000 employees operating in 20 domestic and five foreign locations, the release said.
In conjunction with the merger, ITEQ's board of directors will be expanded from seven to nine persons with the addition of two new members designated by Astrotech, the release said.
The transaction is expected to close in early October, the release said.
Astrotech is a domestic supplier of above-ground storage tanks, providing design, construction, inspection and maintenance products and services.

Astrotech's customer base consists of major oil companies, refineries, petrochemical plants, engineering firms, power producers, waste water plants, agricultural markets and pulp and paper companies, the release said.
The merger will build ITEQ's market share and increase market penetration in several key product lines including cryogenic and pressure vessels, stacks and scrubbers, the release said.

Mark Johnson, chairman and chief executive of ITEQ, said, "The merger of Astrotech into ITEQ clearly establishes ITEQ as one of the pre-eminent consolidators in our industry with pro forma annual revenues of approximately $350 million."
